neighbours.label: stating a benefit: ' that' right after 'the advantage/benefit of X is', and the verb save/saves with time, money or space; 'that' after a speech verb and other senses of 'save' stay low
fire: The advantage of a heat pump is that it works in both seasons.
The benefit of this glue is that it dries within minutes.
One advantage of brick walls is that they need little upkeep.
The main benefit of the new route is that it avoids the bridge.
A big advantage of canned beans is that they keep for years.
A shared printer saves money and desk space in a small office.
Cooking in batches can save time on busy weekdays.
The folding frame saves space in a narrow hallway.
quiet: The engineer said that a heat pump works in both seasons.
The label shows that this glue dries within minutes.
The brick walls that they built need little upkeep.
The driver knew that the new route avoids the bridge.
She heard that canned beans keep for years.
A shared printer costs money and takes desk space in a small office.
The keeper made two fine saves late on busy match days.
The folding frame stands in a narrow hallway.

notes: Card: ' that' x8 ('The advantage of repetition codes is ⟦that⟧'), ' saves' x5, ' save' x3, ' saving' x2, ' saved', ' reduce'. Probes: 'advantage … is that' 0.91, 'benefit … is that' 0.69, 'problem … is that' 0.46, 'reason is that' 0.39, 'save time' 0.52, 'saves a great deal of money' 0.47, 'reduce costs' 0.43, 'saves water' 0.30; 'said that' 0.01, goalkeeper 'saves' 0.00, 'saved a child' 0.04. So the 'is that' part is wider than benefits (any 'the N of X is that'), strongest for advantage/benefit.
